subject: Neurology
vignette: A 74-year-old man has progressive short-term memory loss and cortical atrophy consistent with a neurodegenerative dementia. Autopsy demonstrates degeneration of cholinergic neurons whose cell bodies are located in the basal nucleus of Meynert in the forebrain.
question: A decrease in acetylcholine from the basal nucleus of Meynert is classically associated with which disease?
explanation_correct: In Alzheimer disease, acetylcholine is decreased due to degeneration of cholinergic neurons in the basal nucleus of Meynert (forebrain). Acetylcholine is also reduced in Huntington disease. By contrast, dopamine is decreased in Parkinson disease and increased in schizophrenia; depression is associated with decreased norepinephrine and serotonin.

explanation_incorrect.A: Parkinson disease features decreased dopamine from the substantia nigra, not a primary acetylcholine deficit.
explanation_incorrect.B: Schizophrenia is associated with increased dopamine activity, not decreased acetylcholine.
explanation_incorrect.D: Depression is linked to decreased norepinephrine (locus ceruleus) and serotonin (raphe).
explanation_incorrect.E: Anxiety is associated with increased norepinephrine and decreased serotonin and GABA, not a Meynert acetylcholine deficit.

educationalObjective: Alzheimer disease features decreased acetylcholine from the basal nucleus of Meynert.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A 68-year-old man has a resting tremor, bradykinesia, and cogwheel rigidity. Imaging and pathology show loss of pigmented neurons in the midbrain. A second patient has hallucinations and delusions attributed to excessive dopaminergic transmission.
question: Decreased dopamine synthesis in the ventral tegmentum/substantia nigra is characteristic of which disease?
explanation_correct: Dopamine is synthesized in the ventral tegmental area and substantia nigra pars compacta of the midbrain. It is decreased in Parkinson disease (degeneration of the nigrostriatal pathway) and increased in schizophrenia. Alzheimer disease features decreased acetylcholine, while Huntington disease features decreased acetylcholine and GABA.

explanation_incorrect.A: Schizophrenia is associated with increased, not decreased, dopamine activity.
explanation_incorrect.B: Alzheimer disease involves decreased acetylcholine from the basal nucleus of Meynert.
explanation_incorrect.C: Huntington disease involves decreased acetylcholine and GABA in the basal ganglia.
explanation_incorrect.D: Anxiety involves increased norepinephrine and decreased serotonin and GABA, not a dopamine deficit.

educationalObjective: Dopamine from the VTA/SNc is decreased in Parkinson disease and increased in schizophrenia.

subject: Neurology
vignette: A research team is comparing neurotransmitter levels in several neuropsychiatric conditions. They are specifically examining norepinephrine from the locus ceruleus, serotonin from the raphe nuclei, and GABA from the nucleus accumbens in anxiety, depression, and Huntington disease.
question: Which statement regarding these neurotransmitter changes is correct?

options.text: Norepinephrine from the locus ceruleus is decreased in anxiety
Norepinephrine from the locus ceruleus is increased in anxiety and decreased in depression
Serotonin from the raphe nuclei is increased in depression
GABA in the nucleus accumbens is increased in anxiety
Norepinephrine is synthesized in the raphe nuclei, while serotonin comes from the locus ceruleus

explanation_correct: Norepinephrine, synthesized in the locus ceruleus of the pons, is increased in anxiety and decreased in depression. Serotonin from the raphe nuclei is decreased in both anxiety and depression. GABA in the nucleus accumbens is decreased in anxiety and in Huntington disease.

explanation_incorrect.A: Norepinephrine is increased, not decreased, in anxiety.
explanation_incorrect.C: Serotonin from the raphe nuclei is decreased, not increased, in depression.
explanation_incorrect.D: GABA in the nucleus accumbens is decreased, not increased, in anxiety.
explanation_incorrect.E: The sources are reversed: norepinephrine comes from the locus ceruleus and serotonin from the raphe nuclei.

educationalObjective: NE (locus ceruleus) rises in anxiety and falls in depression; serotonin and GABA generally fall in anxiety/depression.
